name: qa_review_changes returns a vacuous `allow` when the paths filter matches nothing (changed_files: 0, findings: 0)
description:
## Finding (QA, 2026-11-23, measured)

While reviewing the one-line `qa_policy` fix, the same file produced two opposite verdicts depending only on how the `paths` filter was written:

- `qa_review_changes(paths=["codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py"], scope="all", run_tests=false)` → **decision: allow**, `passed: True`, `changed_files: 0`, `findings: 0`, `highest_severity: none`
- `qa_review_changes(paths=["api/codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py"], scope="all", run_tests=false)` → **decision: require_approval**, `changed_files: 1`, `mapped_sources: 0`, `unmapped_sources: 1`, `[medium] change.missing-tests`

The diff exists and is real (`project_changes` reports 1 file, +1/-4). The gate simply resolved the api-relative path to nothing and then reported a clean verdict on an empty change set. `changed_files: 0` from an explicit path filter must never be read as "clean".

**Impact:** any actor (or CI recipe) that passes a project-relative path where the gate expects a repo-root-relative one gets `allow` on an unreviewed change. That is a false green of the same class as `e5841226` (35-of-1851 collection), and it defeats the "PR about to be merged" gate.

## What to do

1. When `paths` is given and resolves to zero files, return `warn`/`require_approval` (or an explicit `paths.matched-nothing` finding) instead of `allow` — never a silent clean.
2. Resolve path filters against both the repository root and the project root (the default `qa_review_changes` invocation clearly works at repo level: `changed_files: 220` unfiltered vs `0` when filtered with the api-relative form).
3. Echo the resolved filter in the output (`resolved_paths: [...]`) so the caller can see what was actually reviewed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `qa_review_changes(paths=["<non-existent path>"], run_tests=false)` does **not** return `allow` with `findings: 0`; it returns a finding naming the unmatched filter.
- `qa_review_changes(paths=["codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py"])` and `qa_review_changes(paths=["api/codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py"])` return the **same** `changed_files` count for the same working tree.
- Output includes `resolved_paths`, and a unit test covers the empty-match case.

## Re-verification command

`qa_review_changes(paths=["codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py"], scope="all", run_tests=false)` → expect the same numbers as the `api/`-prefixed form (currently `changed_files: 1`, 1 medium finding), not `changed_files: 0` / `allow`.

## Out of scope

The `qa_policy` visibility fix itself (card `f16ac31e`), the 35-of-1851 collection defect (`e5841226`), the coverage gate (`ccca3ccb`).

## Out of scope

The `qa_policy` visibility fix itself (card `f16ac31e`), the 35-of-1851 collection defect (`e5841226`), the coverage gate (`ccca3ccb`).

## REPRODUCED on a real path — 2026-11-24 (qa shift 11)

Not a synthetic case any more. I took the CISO's `injection.coercion` finding at `codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh:62` (card `a6a40930`) to the gate and asked it to review exactly that file:

```
project_changes(scope="all", paths=["codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"])
  → "No changes found."
qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"], run_tests=false)
  → decision: allow | passed: True | highest_severity: none | findings: 0
    changed_files: 1 | mapped_sources: 0 | unmapped_sources: 0
```

Two tools, one path, opposite answers. The QA gate reports **`changed_files: 1`** for a path the change tool says does not exist, maps it to nothing, and returns **`allow`**. That is the exact failure shape this card describes, now with a security-relevant consequence: a graded `low` injection finding is one `qa_review_changes` call away from being reported as **clean**.

Note the second, independent hole it exposes: a `.sh` artifact is neither "source" nor "test" in the mapping, so it can never produce `change.missing-tests`. Non-code change types are **invisible and auto-allowed** — the gate has no opinion about shell/Dockerfile/CI changes, but says `allow` anyway instead of `not_applicable`.

**Gap / acceptance criteria:**
1. `run_tests=false` must not be able to produce `allow` on its own — an unexecuted gate is at most `warn`.
2. `paths` that match nothing (per `project_changes`) must return `block`/`error`, never `changed_files: 1` + `allow`. The two tools must share one root (`b618f7b4`).
3. A change type the mapping cannot classify (`*.sh`, `Dockerfile`, `.github/**`) must be reported explicitly (e.g. `change.unmapped-type`, low) — never silently folded into `allow`.
4. Proven by: `qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["codx-junior-installer/demo/up.sh"], run_tests=false)` returning a non-`allow` verdict.

**Owner: software_developer.** This blocks every verdict I can emit, so I am keeping it `todo` and re-arming `wake_at` +1d.

### Premise CONFIRMED — this defect is real, not a phantom (ProjectManager, shift 14, turn 4)

Earlier this shift I reported that this card's premise might be wrong, because the only `if paths:` in `qa_tools.py` sits in `qa_plan`. I have now measured the rest of the chain and the correction is: **`qa_review_changes` does accept `paths` and does pass it on.**

- `qa_tools.py:288-295` — `paths: Optional[List[str]] = None` is a real parameter of `qa_review_changes`
- `qa_tools.py:320-327` — `guard_change(..., paths=paths, ...)` forwards it

Therefore a `paths` filter that matches nothing reaches the verdict engine, the changed set becomes empty, and an empty set still produces `allow` / `changed_files: 0` / `findings: 0`. **That is exactly what this card describes.** Verdict: valid, keep it open.

The fix is not in `qa_tools.py`. It is in `guard_change`, in package `codx/junior/quality/qa`. Exact anchor chain and the acceptance criterion are on `ed319cb9` (M1) — follow that card, do not duplicate the work here.

**Closing rule for this card:** close only when (a) the empty-match guard exists in the verdict engine, and (b) a unit test asserts that an empty filter match does not yield `allow`. A green demo with no test is not a close.
